subject: Order Form: Security exhibit — inspection boundaries, pen-test language, and evidence timetable
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@centricahealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@centricahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order Form: Security exhibit questions

Markus —

Thanks for the draft Order Form. A couple of items we need clarified on the security exhibit before procurement can proceed:

- Scope: Centrica is comfortable with SOC 2 Type II evidence (reports and control summaries). We are concerned about open-ended "inspection rights" language that could imply full production access. Can we limit inspection to evidence snapshot delivery and scoped reviews?
- Pen test: We generally prefer partner-led pen-tests with redacted results versus direct production penetration. If you require on-demand pen-tests, we need to understand the notice window and pre-approved testing windows.
- Evidence cadence: Can you propose an evidence cadence that balances our compliance team needs with your operational constraints? Monthly snapshots + quarterly deeper reviews would be ideal.

Appreciate your proposed language and any redlines so procurement can move to a PO.

Thanks,
Amy Chen
Head of Information Security
Centrica Health

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@centricahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-24T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Security exhibit questions

Amy —

Thanks for the clear list. I attached a focused redline (security_exhibit_markus_redline_v1.docx) that attempts to reconcile two priorities: (1) provide Centrica the evidence needed for your SOC 2 compliance, and (2) keep inspection scope operationally bounded so our infra team doesn't have indefinite obligations. High level:

- Replace "inspection rights" with "evidence and scoped review rights," and define what constitutes a review (forensic on-call vs. artifact delivery).
- Pen tests: propose joint testing windows (30-45 day advance notice, mutually agreed scope) and acceptance of vendor-led redacted reports in lieu of direct production tests.
- Cadence: propose monthly artifact snapshots (control matrix + key logs) and a quarterly 2-hour technical review call; ad-hoc deeper dives require 30-day notice unless part of the annual SOC 2 cadence.

Can I ask Legal (Laura) to give language for the inspection carveouts and Karthik/Vanessa for any commercial concessions we should offer (credits, limited SLA carveout) if Centrica insists on broader access?

Markus
VP Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: security_exhibit_markus_redline_v1.docx (Word doc — redlines marked)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Amy Chen <amy.chen@centricahealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-25T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Security exhibit questions

Markus / Amy —

I reviewed Markus's redline and Amy's asks. Proposed legal position below (summary + suggested clause text attached):

Summary: We will agree to:
- Replace generic "audit/inspection rights" with a defined "Evidence Review and Inspection" clause.
- Limit inspections to: (a) delivery of SOC 2 Type II reports and control mappings; (b) scheduled technical review sessions where Redwood provides redacted artifacts and scoped logs; (c) a jointly scheduled test window for penetration testing subject to safety constraints.

Key elements to include in the clause:
- 45-day written notice for any inspection beyond routine artifact delivery.
- Penetration testing: Redwood will accept vendor-conducted pen-tests with redacted technical output as an alternative to direct production testing; customer-led tests permitted only within an agreed staging environment or under strict test-plan and rollback commitments.
- Data access: no direct access to customer data stores unless expressly required and then only under a supervised evidence-collection process.

I've attached a one-page suggested clause and a SOC2 summary we can share with the Centrica team to expedite procurement. If we need to provide a concession, my recommended commercial levers are: one-time credit if Centrica requires a dedicated pen-test window, or a 30-day extended commit on an annual order to cover the operational lift.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2-Summary-Centrica.pdf (PDF — control mapping + what we can share)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@centricahealth.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-27T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Security exhibit questions

Amy —

Appreciate the cooperative tone here. Operational proposal (to align with Laura's legal language):

- Evidence cadence: monthly automated artifact package (SOC2 control mapping + service config snapshot) delivered via secure link; quarterly 60-minute technical review (calendar invite + agenda 7 days prior).
- Pen-test handling: if Centrica wants vendor-led testing, Redwood will provide a redacted summary and remediation timeline. For customer-requested tests, we offer a staged environment for testing within a 45-day scheduling window.
- Escalation: if Centrica identifies a control regression during review, we commit to a 10-business-day remediation plan for P1/P2 items and a formal root-cause write-up for anything classified as a security incident.

Commercial concessions: open to a single goodwill credit (5% of first-year committed spend) if Centrica requires an on-prem/staged pen-test and acceptance of the report in lieu of redacted vendor output.

Next step: if Amy is OK, I'll have our contracts team send the revised language and a short redline summary for Centrica's counsel.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jack Field (CPO) <jack.field@centricahealth.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@centricahealth.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@centricahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-31T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Security exhibit questions

Markus / Laura / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. Centrica is aligned with the SOC2-based evidence flow and the staged test approach, but two asks before procurement proceeds:

1) Test window: we need a guaranteed annual joint testing window (we'll pick a week; Redwood to confirm availability) rather than ad-hoc requests. That gives our audit team assurance.
2) Evidence retention: can Redwood commit to retaining the monthly artifact snapshots for a minimum of 12 months accessible via a secure portal?

If you can confirm those points and include the 45-day notice in the doc, procurement will push the PO through next week.

Regards,
Jack Field
Chief Product Officer
Centrica Health

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Jack Field (CPO) <jack.field@centricahealth.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@centricahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@centricahealth.com
Date: 2026-09-01T14:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Security exhibit questions

Jack / Amy —

Confirmed items and next steps:

- Annual joint test window: agreed. Redwood will propose three possible weeks in Q1 2027; Centrica picks one. We'll lock that into the Order Form appendix.
- Evidence retention: Redwood will retain monthly artifact snapshots for 12 months and provide access via our secure Share link; we will include the retention commitment in the redline.
- 45-day notice: we'll keep the 45-day notice for non-routine inspections in the legal clause.

Attached: final redline will be posted to the DocuSign link below; Laura will do one last pass on the clause language and Vanessa will confirm the proposed commercial credit path if Centrica requests a dedicated pen-test.

Action items:
- Laura: final clause and insert into the Order Form appendix (by EOD 9/2).
- Vanessa: confirm commercial credit wording (by EOD 9/2).
- Amy / Jack: sign off on the high-level commitments (annual window + 12-mo retention) and we'll circulate the DocuSign.

Redwood Inference
